solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Italy never supported English manoeuvre

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that is supported sits underneath the piece holding it up

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
ne'er is the poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: A tourist complains that Italy never backed some English diplomatic move.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supported' means placed below, so I and NE'ER come after ENG.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer something is to contrive or arrange it cleverly, which is what manoeuvring as a verb means.

clue.text: Lift arm and grab gold perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a word turns it upside down, so its letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: a gun is a weapon, an arm
to get something is to grab or obtain it

explanation.surface: An instruction to raise your arm and snatch some gold, perhaps in a heist.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a lump of precious metal, gold being the classic example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Fine French raised more without trouble

indicators.note: in a down entry raising a word means its letters run upwards

parts.note: bon is French for good or fine
other can mean additional or further, as in 'other copies'

explanation.surface: Someone says fine, in French, and asks for more without any fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom said when something is easily done, meaning it caused no difficulty at all.

clue.text: Fuss at home over judge? Neighbours do it

indicators.note: the fuss-at-home letters are spread over the judge's letter, so it sits inside them

parts.note: ado is a fuss or commotion
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A domestic row over a legal decision, the sort of thing neighbours get into.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful one: properties that are neighbours adjoin each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbouring houses share a boundary, which is exactly what touching or bordering on each other means.

clue.text: Loyalists are victorious at start and finish

indicators.note: this tells us the winning letters go at the front of the loyalists' abbreviation

parts.note: to win is to be victorious
the DUP, Democratic Unionist Party, is a Northern Irish loyalist party

explanation.surface: Northern Irish loyalists win from first to last.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, loyal to the British Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind up a meeting or business is to bring it to an end, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Duchy was given up after conflict

indicators.note: the reversed word follows the conflict's letters

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: in a down entry giving a word up sends its letters upwards

explanation.surface: A duchy was surrendered once fighting ended.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duchy of Warsaw was a Polish state Napoleon set up in 1807, in keeping with the puzzle's Napoleonic theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish capital was the seat of a Napoleonic duchy, so the city's name stands for that state.

clue.text: Like allies, hemmed in but not united

indicators.note: this says the following letter is to be left out

parts.note: bounded means enclosed or hemmed in by limits
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Allies boxed in, though no longer united, an ironic picture of a coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: Allies are joined by a treaty or pact, so they are tied together, held by a bond.

clue.text: Activities popular among Pomeranians, say

indicators.note: the popular letters go among, inside, the dogs' letters

parts.note: Pomeranians are a toy breed, examples of dogs
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Pastimes that catch on with Pomeranians and similar lapdogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Doings is an informal plural for things someone has been doing, their goings-on or activities.

clue.text: Brought life back to grass covering new 11 in project

indicators.note: the grass's letters are wrapped round everything that follows

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: the rearranged cross-referenced word goes in the project's letters

parts.note: to jut is to stick out, project

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: the answer to clue 11 across, a sail of a windmill

explanation.surface: A garden revived by laying grass over a new vane in a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges VANE into VENA, which goes 'in' JUT to make JUVENAT; REED, 'covering', splits round that.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejuvenate is to make young or vigorous again, restoring life and freshness.

clue.text: One alliance involved Vatican and Berlin, say

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the alliance's letters involve, enfold, the Vatican's letter

parts.note: a ring is a group or alliance, as in a spy ring
V is the international vehicle code for Vatican City

explanation.surface: A wartime-sounding pact between the Vatican and Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berlin' looks like the German capital but is the songwriter Irving Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: The songwriter Berlin had this first name, so he is an example of someone so called.

clue.text: Prudent European army chief captured one retreating

indicators.note: the chief's letters hold the reversed word captive inside

parts.note: CIC stands for commander-in-chief

indicators.note: retreating says the word for one is read backwards

parts.note: mono is a prefix meaning one

explanation.surface: A careful European general takes a prisoner who is falling back.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic can mean thrifty or sparing with money, a prudent use of resources.

clue.text: Sail rejected by the navy

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sail turned down by the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A windmill's sail is one of the arms or blades that the wind turns.

clue.text: Risky move in the past secured north Germany

parts.note: to touch someone is to move them emotionally

indicators.note: the past's letters hold the next letters fast inside

parts.note: ago means in the past, as in 'long ago'
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A hazardous move from history that secured northern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' looks like a noun in the definition but is a verb, to affect emotionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Something touch and go is precarious, its outcome uncertain, so it is dangerous or chancy.

clue.text: Town crier fussed over place for Pope's headgear

indicators.note: the rearranged letters lie over, around, the abbreviation for place
letters that are fussed over are fiddled with, worked into a new order

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses

explanation.surface: A town crier makes a fuss about where the Pope's hat should go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fussed' rearranges TOWN CRIER into TRIECROWN, which goes 'over' PL, split as TRI and ECROWN.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal tiara, a three-tiered crown once worn by popes, is known by this name.

clue.text: Papers inspired old King George to carry on

indicators.note: inspired literally means breathed in, so the papers take the next letters inside

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: The newspapers prompted old King George to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To progress is to move forward or continue, to keep going with something.

clue.text: Bitter dispute arising over land borders

definitions.text: Bitter dispute arising over land borders

indicators.note: the reversed letters go over, around, the edge letters of land
in a down entry arising means the words run upwards, read backwards

parts.note: raw can mean bitter, as a raw wind
a row is a quarrel or dispute

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A savage conflict breaking out over territorial frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns RAW and ROW together into WORWAR, which goes 'over' LD, the borders of land. The whole clue also describes such a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A global war is the ultimate bitter dispute, and both great wars began over territory and frontiers.

clue.text: Nervous leader ignored criticism

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here left out

parts.note: fearful means nervous or afraid

explanation.surface: An anxious leader brushed off the criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a lengthy scolding or telling-off is getting this, a colloquial word for a reprimand.

clue.text: Minister tackled navy's big guns

indicators.note: the minister's letters tackle, grab hold of, the navy's letter

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman, a minister of a cathedral
N is the abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes on the navy's heavy artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big guns' may suggest important people, but the plural of this artillery piece is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannon are heavy artillery pieces, and the word serves as its own plural.

clue.text: Like meetings here in the periphery 200 years ago

definitions.text: Like meetings here in the periphery 200 years ago

parts.words: Like meetings here in the periphery 200 years ago
parts.note: a cryptic pointer to themed meetings two centuries back, held in person with the parties confronting one another

explanation.surface: A historical note about meetings held round the edges two centuries ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the puzzle's Napoleonic theme and on entries round the grid's edge; the answer describes opponents meeting directly.
explanation.definitionFit: Meetings held in person, with the participants directly confronting one another, are described by this phrase.

clue.text: One-time good guys oddly excluded flight

parts.note: ex means former, one-time

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are left out, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Former heroes, strangely, were left out of the flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like a plane journey but means escape.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is a mass departure, a fleeing from somewhere, as the Israelites fled Egypt.

clue.text: Avoid uneasy peace to protect Sweden

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround and shield the next letter
uneasy signals letters that are unsettled into another order

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Steer clear of an uneasy truce meant to protect Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneasy' rearranges PEACE into ECAPE, which splits round S, 'to protect' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape a danger or duty is to avoid it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Second-in-command galloped around on it?

indicators.note: the running letters go around the chosen letter

parts.note: ran is a synonym of galloped, moved fast

indicators.note: the second letter in the following word is picked

explanation.surface: A deputy commander riding around on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-in-command' looks like a deputy but gives O, the second letter of 'command'. The whole clue hints at a horse to gallop on.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse with a coat of mixed white and coloured hairs, something one gallops on.

clue.text: As expected, force abandoned missing target

indicators.note: abandoned says the following letter is dropped

parts.note: off course means straying from the target
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: The armed force gave up after missing its target, as everyone predicted.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course is said of something naturally to be expected, as in 'naturally, certainly'.

clue.text: Initially Castlereagh, say, curbed uproar, giving ground

indicators.note: this picks the first letter of the following word
the example letters curb, hem in, the uproar's letters

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'say' means here
a din is a loud noise, an uproar

explanation.surface: Castlereagh quelled a disturbance as the opposition gave way.
explanation.walkthrough: Castlereagh was the British Foreign Secretary in the Napoleonic era.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceding is yielding or surrendering territory, literally giving ground to another.

clue.text: The French limited their assents for Boney's wife (after Marie)

indicators.note: the article's letters set limits round the next letters

parts.note: le is a French word for the
oui is French for yes, so French assents are ouis

explanation.surface: The French rationed their yeses for Napoleon's second wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Boney is a nickname for Napoleon; his second wife was the Archduchess Marie Louise.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's second empress was Marie Louise of Austria, so this name follows Marie.

clue.text: Injure King in country Napoleon invaded

indicators.note: the king's letter goes in the country's name

parts.note: Napoleon invaded Spain in 1808, leading to the Peninsular War
R stands for rex, king

explanation.surface: A king hurt in a country Napoleon conquered.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprain a joint is to twist and injure it, a specific kind of hurt.
